rawFindings.title: Setting process.exitCode without stopping server start on load errors leads to unexpected behavior
rawFindings.explanation: In the server start function, when load errors are detected, the code sets process.exitCode = 1 but then immediately sends SIGINT to the process. However, this does not stop the server start sequence early and may lead to inconsistent server state or multiple stop attempts. Setting the exit code without terminating or stopping further processing may cause unpredictable behavior during startup failures.
rawFindings.suggestion: Immediately return after setting process.exitCode=1 and emitting SIGINT, or refactor to properly stop server initialization flow when load errors occur.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: When the server starts with load errors present, process.exitCode is set to 1 but server start continues, potentially causing multiple exits or inconsistent state.

rawFindings.title: Anonymous SIGINT handler on processWrapper leads to duplicated logic and potential inconsistency
rawFindings.explanation: The SIGINT listener on processWrapper was changed from a direct function reference (disconnectBrowsers) to an anonymous function calling disconnectBrowsers with process.exitCode. This can lead to subtle differences in behavior because the original handler passed the event arguments directly, but now the handler ignores the SIGINT event arguments and reuses process.exitCode. This minor change might add unnecessary indirection or prevent future signal argument usage.
rawFindings.suggestion: Keep the SIGINT handler as processWrapper.on('SIGINT', disconnectBrowsers) to preserve existing semantics unless passing the exit code via a wrapper function is strictly required.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: SIGINT events on processWrapper are handled differently and may affect signal handling behavior.
